一

Itinerary

Day by day, as it stands today. Candidate plans are labeled as such — nothing here is booked unless it says so.

Wed · Mar 3

Jeannie heads out early

Jeannie flies ORD → Tokyo Narita solo, two days ahead of the pack, and settles in at the Hotel New Otani Tokyo Garden Tower. Extra sleep and a head start on marathon week.

Flight — ticketedSeat 19A · Premium Economy
Transportation

ORD → Narita (NRT) by air, then into the city: Narita Express (N'EX) to Tokyo Station (~1 hr), transfer to the Marunouchi Line to Akasaka-mitsuke, then a short walk to the Hotel New Otani in Kioicho. Simpler with bags: the Airport Limousine Bus runs from Narita direct to the Hotel New Otani — no transfer. A taxi for the last hop from Tokyo Station is the fallback.

Fri · Mar 5

Todd + the kids depart Chicago

Todd, Natalie, Rory, Dash, and Phoebe take JAL flight JL9 from O'Hare to Haneda — an overnight flight that lands the next day, Sat Mar 6 at 5:50 p.m. local time. Base once they land: the family Airbnb in Akasaka, about 200 m from Akasaka-mitsuke Station.

Flight — ticketedLands Sat Mar 6 · 5:50 p.m. HND
Transportation

O'Hare (ORD) → Haneda (HND): JL9 nonstop, departing Fri Mar 5 and arriving Sat Mar 6 at 5:50 p.m. local time. The Haneda → Akasaka transfer is covered under Sat Mar 6 below.

Sat · Mar 6

Arrival in Tokyo — JL9 lands 5:50 p.m.

Not a free day — Todd and the kids land at Haneda at 5:50 p.m. local time on JL9. It's an arrival evening: get to the Akasaka Airbnb, drop the bags, and head out for dinner around 7:30 p.m. — then keep it early ahead of marathon day tomorrow. Jeannie, in Tokyo since Mar 3, meets the family at the Airbnb (not the airport) and walks to dinner with everyone.

Flight JL9 — lands 5:50 p.m. at HanedaArrival eveningJeannie meets the family at the Airbnb
Dining — arrival night, ~7:30 p.m.

Three easy options, all a few minutes' walk from the Airbnb after the bags are dropped:

  1. Sushi no Midori Akasaka — ~3-minute walk, open Saturdays until 9:30 p.m. Popular nigiri and sashimi sets the kids will love. For Jeannie: sashimi and rice are fine — just skip the regular soy sauce or ask for tamari. Be ready for a short Saturday-night wait.
  2. Yakiniku Kintan Akasaka — ~3-minute walk, open Saturdays until 10:45 p.m. Casual wagyu where the kids grill their own meat at the table. For Jeannie: stick to the salt-style cuts, since the tare sauces usually contain soy sauce.
  3. Gusto Akasaka-mitsuke — ~6-minute walk, open until 11 p.m. Big menu with English touch-panel ordering and no wait — the zero-effort fallback if everyone's too wiped out to think.
Transportation

Haneda (HND) → Akasaka Airbnb: landing 5:50 p.m. at Terminal 3 — allow time for immigration and bags, then head into the city. By train: Keikyu Line to Shinagawa, JR Yamanote Line to Yurakucho, then Marunouchi Line to Akasaka-mitsuke (about 45–55 min) and the ~200 m walk to the Airbnb. With five people and bags on arrival evening, two taxis or a pre-booked van direct from Haneda to Akasaka (~30–40 min by road) is the easier call. No sightseeing this evening — just check in and rest.

Sun · Mar 7

Tokyo Marathon — Jeannie races

Jeannie auto-qualified through the Age Group World Championships rankings — no lottery, no tour package needed. The family cheers her on, then celebrates with the trip's one big Tokyo restaurant night: monjayaki in Tsukishima at Monja Takarajima, the only monja shop in the neighborhood with a gluten-free (rice-flour) version, so Jeannie can eat what everyone else is eating.

Marathon — qualifiedDinner pick made · reservation pending
Transportation

To the start: Akasaka-mitsuke → Marunouchi Line to Shinjuku, then follow the race-morning flow to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building start in Nishi-Shinjuku — leave early, stations near the start get very crowded. Spectating / finish: Marunouchi Line to Tokyo Station for the Gyoko-dori finish. To dinner in Tsukishima: from the Tokyo Station finish, it's a short walk to Yurakucho Station, then the Yurakucho Line direct to Tsukishima Station and ~3 min on foot to Monja Takarajima (3-5-4 Tsukishima). Coming from Akasaka instead: Marunouchi Line to Ginza, transfer to the Yurakucho Line to Tsukishima.

Mon · Mar 8

Anime afternoon + cooking class Candidate day

Two candidate plans that can combine: the Shibuya–Harajuku anime run (both One Piece Mugiwara stores, Jump Shop, Nintendo Tokyo, the Pokémon Center, and the Capyneko capybara café) and an early-evening sushi-making class at Mayuko's Little Kitchen, where dinner is what you make. Slots still to be locked — Sun Mar 7 afternoon is the alternate for the anime run.

Dash's One Piece routeMayuko inquiry sent Oct 14 · awaiting reply
Transportation

Akasaka → Shibuya: Ginza Line direct from Akasaka-mitsuke to Shibuya Station (~10 min), then walk to Shibuya Parco and MAGNET by SHIBUYA109. Shibuya → Harajuku: JR Yamanote Line one stop to Harajuku Station, or walk it in ~24 min; Harajuku's Mugiwara Store (Harakado) and Capyneko on Takeshita Street are ~5 min apart on foot. To Mayuko's (Sendagaya): JR Chuo-Sobu Line to Sendagaya Station, then a short walk — or a taxi from Harajuku if the class start is tight. Home: Ginza Line from Shibuya or Marunouchi/Ginza lines back to Akasaka-mitsuke.

Tue · Mar 9

Tokyo DisneySea — full day

The last full Tokyo day is a full day at Tokyo DisneySea in Urayasu — the only DisneySea park in the world, and a park you can only do in Japan. All six, open to close, before the move to the mountains tomorrow. Anything from earlier in the week that still needs a slot (Nakano Broadway, Akihabara, Animate Ikebukuro) folds into the lighter days around it.

DisneySea — Tue Mar 9Park tickets — still pending, not yet purchased
Transportation

Akasaka → DisneySea: walk to Akasaka-mitsuke, Marunouchi Line to Tokyo Station, then follow the signs (it's a long underground walk inside the station) to the JR Keiyo Line and ride to Maihama Station (~15 min). From Maihama, take the Disney Resort Line monorail one stop to Tokyo DisneySea Station — or walk ~10 min to the gates. About 60–75 min door to gates, so start early for rope drop. Home: reverse it — Disney Resort Line to Maihama, Keiyo Line to Tokyo Station, Marunouchi Line to Akasaka-mitsuke.

Wed · Mar 10

Tokyo → Shibu Onsen · Kokuya ryokan

Train to Nagano and on to Shibu Onsen for a night at historic Kokuya — two Take rooms and the Shinshu Beef dinner plan. On the doorstep: the snow-monkey hike, Tamamura Honten's sake storehouse and gallery (~0.3 km), and Onsenji Temple up its stone steps (~0.4 km). Zenkoji Temple in Nagano City fits on the way if timing allows.

Stay — booked¥238,260 (~$1,506)Snow monkeys
Transportation

Akasaka → Tokyo Station: Marunouchi Line direct from Akasaka-mitsuke. Tokyo → Nagano: Hokuriku Shinkansen (~1 hr 20 min, reserved seats for six — still to book). Nagano → Yudanaka: Nagano Electric Railway (Nagaden) local line (~45 min). Yudanaka → Shibu Onsen / Kokuya: short local bus, ryokan pickup, or taxi (~10 min). Once at Kokuya, Shibu itself is on foot — Tamamura Honten ~0.3 km, Onsenji ~0.4 km; the snow-monkey park is a bus/taxi to the trailhead plus the forest walk in.

Thu · Mar 11

Ski day · Shiga Kogen Prince Hotel West

Rent skis and ski all day at Shiga Kogen, then sleep slopeside at the Prince Hotel West — two rooms, dinner and breakfast included. Special requests are on file: adjoining rooms, and the twin beds pushed together in Room 2.

Stay — booked & verified¥116,650 (~$738) due at propertySki rental — pending
Transportation

Shibu Onsen → Shiga Kogen: Nagaden express bus from the Shibu / Yudanaka area up to Shiga Kogen (~40–50 min in winter), getting off at the Prince Hotel West area (Hasuike / Sun Valley side) — check the hotel's own shuttle timing against the bus when you check out of Kokuya. During the day: ski lifts and the resort's local shuttle buses between areas; the hotel is slopeside, so it's ski-in from the door. No car needed.

Fri – Sat · Mar 12 – 13

Kyoto

Two nights in Kyoto to close the trip. The days are deliberately open — the lodging is the trip's biggest remaining booking (see Still Pending).

Lodging — not yet booked
Transportation

Shiga Kogen → Nagano Station (Fri Mar 12): Nagaden express bus back down the mountain (~1 hr). Nagano → Kyoto: by train via Kanazawa — Hokuriku Shinkansen to Kanazawa, then the Thunderbird limited express to Kyoto Station (roughly 4 hrs end to end; the alternative via Tokyo is longer). Pick the departure once train reservations are booked. Zenkoji in Nagano City fits this transfer window if timing allows. In Kyoto: taxi or subway/bus from Kyoto Station to the lodging (once booked), then city buses, the Karasuma and Tozai subway lines, and walking between sights.

Sun · Mar 14

Everyone home together

All six fly the same route home: JL112 from Osaka Itami to Haneda (10:25 a.m.), connecting to JL10 Haneda → O'Hare, 1:10 p.m. – 11:00 a.m.

Flights — ticketedAll 6 on both legs
Transportation

Kyoto → Osaka Itami (ITM): the direct airport limousine bus from Kyoto Station to Itami is the simplest move for six people plus bags (~55 min) — plan to leave Kyoto by about 7:30 a.m. for the 10:25 a.m. flight; the train alternative is JR/Hankyu into Osaka plus a bus or monorail hop to Itami. At Haneda: JL112 arrives at the domestic terminal — follow the international-transfer signs (free shuttle bus / Keikyu-Monorail hop) to Terminal 3 for JL10. Haneda → O'Hare: JL10, 1:10 p.m. – 11:00 a.m. same day.

Upgrade watch — where it stands

Premium Economy exists on the outbound, but American's Executive Platinum desk confirmed (Oct 13 call) there are no instant cash upgrade offers on these miles-booked tickets — so the only real path to Business is cancel-and-rebook if a fare worth jumping on appears. Daily checks on both directions and a weekly Business price check are running, and any threshold-beating deal gets flagged. Nothing to decide today.

四

Dining

Every pick below was checked for a gluten-free path for Jeannie.

Arrival night — dinner near the Akasaka Airbnb Options · Sat Mar 6

Saturday Mar 6, ~7:30 p.m. — after JL9 lands at Haneda at 5:50 p.m. and bags are dropped at the Airbnb. Jeannie meets the family at the Airbnb, and everyone walks to dinner together. Three easy options, all a few minutes away:

Sushi no Midori Akasaka — ~3-minute walk; open Saturdays until 9:30 p.m. Popular nigiri and sashimi sets the kids will love. For Jeannie: sashimi and rice are fine — skip the regular soy sauce or ask for tamari. Expect a short Saturday-night wait.
Yakiniku Kintan Akasaka — ~3-minute walk; open Saturdays until 10:45 p.m. Casual wagyu the kids grill themselves at the table. For Jeannie: stick to the salt-style cuts — the tare sauces usually contain soy sauce.
Gusto Akasaka-mitsuke — ~6-minute walk; open until 11 p.m. Big menu, English touch-panel ordering, no wait — the zero-effort fallback if everyone's too wiped out to think.

Marathon night — Monja Takarajima, Tsukishima Pick made · reserve in Jan

Sunday Mar 7. The family's one Tokyo restaurant night: special but not fancy, in a neighborhood that's new to everyone, with a post-marathon Jeannie who'll be tired and hungry. Takarajima is the only Tsukishima monja shop with gluten-free monjayaki (rice flour), plus GF okonomiyaki — so it's a celebration, not a compromise.

The shortlist — verified alternatives

All checked: open Sundays, gluten-free workable, family-reviewed. Kept in reserve if Takarajima fills up or plans shift.

Coco Nemaru Ginza — ranch-direct wagyu yakiniku (Yamaguchi/Mogami beef), private rooms, English menu, kids welcome. ¥10,000–15,000 pp, Sun 12:30–11:00 p.m. Todd's find, and the strongest Ushihachi alternative.
Ushihachi, Ueno — wagyu yakiniku on the 10F of Fundes Ueno, family-friendly booths, English menu. ¥6,000–10,000 pp.
Inakaya, Roppongi — robatayaki theater, the splurge: ¥15,000–20,000 pp + 10% service, counter seats only.
Gonpachi, Nishi-Azabu — the "Kill Bill" restaurant; lively and great with kids, with the caveat that the spectacle outruns the food.

Adults-only option: Bar Centifolia in Azabu-Juban — a 14-seat counter where Yuzo Komai cuts ice with a sword and sets cocktails alight. ~¥4,000–5,000 per drink, opens 8:30 p.m., closed Wednesdays, reservations via TableCheck. A Todd + Jeannie date night (Fri or Sat) if a kid plan comes together.

Off the list for good: Chanko Tomoegata in Ryogoku — permanently closed. The Pokémon restaurant was considered and rejected — a tourist trap that's fun only for superfans.

五

Getting Around

Trains first, everywhere. Taxis only where they genuinely beat the train for six people plus bags.

In Tokyo

The Akasaka Airbnb sits ~200 m from Akasaka-mitsuke Station. The Marunouchi line runs direct to Tokyo Station (about 30–40 min door-to-platform) — the launchpad for marathon morning and every day trip.

Shibuya and Harajuku pair up on foot and by short hops for the anime afternoon: Harajuku → Shibuya is about a 24-minute walk.

DisneySea day (Tue Mar 9): Akasaka-mitsuke → Marunouchi Line to Tokyo Station → JR Keiyo Line to Maihama → Disney Resort Line monorail to Tokyo DisneySea Station. About 60–75 min door to gates — see the Mar 9 itinerary entry for the step-by-step.

六

Things to Do

The fun list — built around Dash's One Piece fandom, the snow monkeys, and one very good ski day.

The Shibuya–Harajuku anime afternoon

Confirmed plan: both One Piece Mugiwara stores in one afternoon — they're different shops, not duplicates. Candidate slots: Sun Mar 7 afternoon (post-marathon, while Jeannie rests) or Mon Mar 8 midday.

  1. Shibuya Crossing, then up to Shibuya Parco 6F — Jump Shop, Nintendo Tokyo, and the Pokémon Center on one floor.
  2. Mugiwara Store Shibuya — 6F MAGNET by SHIBUYA109, 1-23-10 Jinnan. The original main store, renovated Feb 2025; life-sized figures and the Shanks statue that puts his hat on your head. 10 a.m.–9 p.m.
  3. Walk or hop to Harajuku (~24 min on foot).
  4. Mugiwara Store Harajuku — G floor, Tokyu Plaza Harajuku "Harakado", 6-31-21 Jingumae. The ~2 m Gear 5 Luffy statue and Harajuku-exclusive Chopper goods. 11 a.m.–9 p.m.
  5. Capyneko Harajuku — 5 min away on Takeshita Street: capybaras and rescue cats, 40-min session ¥3,850 pp (~$24; ¥23,100 / ~$146 for six, treats ¥550). Reservations required via TableCheck — booking is on the pending list.

Also on the anime list for other days: Nakano Broadway, Akihabara, and the Animate Ikebukuro flagship.

Nagano, beyond the slopes

  • Snow-monkey hike — the onsen-soaking macaques, paired with the Kokuya night (Mar 10–11).
  • Tamamura Honten — sake storehouse, art museum and gallery ~0.3 km from Kokuya: self-serve tastings and craft beer on tap. (Closed Sundays/holidays — we're there Wed/Thu.)
  • Onsenji Temple — Shibu's temple atop its stone steps, ~0.4 km from Kokuya.
  • Zenkoji Temple, Nagano City — if the transfer windows on Mar 10 or Mar 12 cooperate.
  • Ski all day Thu Mar 11 at Shiga Kogen — rental gear still to arrange.

Tokyo DisneySea — Tue Mar 9

A full day at the only DisneySea in the world, on the last full Tokyo day. Mediterranean Harbor, Mysterious Island, and the new Fantasy Springs area are the uniquely-DisneySea draws you can't get at any U.S. park. Tickets are still pending — not yet purchased (see Still Pending); they're date-specific, so Mar 9 is the date to lock.

Watch for in January

One Piece & anime exhibitions — a January check is set for exhibitions running during the Mar 5–9 Tokyo window. January is also when March bookings open up across the board: Mayuko's class dates, Capyneko reservations, and the Takarajima table all land in that same sweep.

Frequently asked questions

Quick answers to the things that come up most — all drawn from what’s already on this page.

How does the form above actually reach Sully?

Submitting opens your own mail app with an email pre-addressed to sully@muse.ai, with your name and message filled in. You still need to press send in your mail app — that’s what delivers it. From there, confirmed info gets added to this page on the next update, and anything that’s a new task gets brought back to Todd in chat.

Why do the flights say “Jeanne” when everywhere else says “Jeannie”?

She goes by Jeannie — that’s the name used everywhere on this page. Her legal name is Jeanne Sullivan, as on her driver’s license and passport, so all flight tickets have to be bought in that name. Her flight card keeps “Jeanne” for exactly that reason; it’s not a typo.

Are the DisneySea tickets bought yet?

Not yet — they’re still pending. Tuesday, March 9 is a full DisneySea day in the itinerary, but tickets for all six haven’t been purchased. They’re date-specific and sold about two months ahead via the official Tokyo Disney Resort site/app, so they’re on the Still Pending list to buy as soon as the Mar 9 window opens.

What’s still left to book?

The big one is Kyoto lodging for Mar 12–14 — the last unbooked stay. Also still open: passport details on the flight bookings, train tickets and seat reservations (Tokyo → Nagano, Nagano → Kyoto, Kyoto → Itami), ski gear rental for Mar 11 at Shiga Kogen, the Mar 7 table at Monja Takarajima, the Capyneko session, and Mayuko’s cooking class. The full grouped list is in Still Pending.

What about gluten-free food for Jeannie?

Every meal on the trip is planned around it — Jeannie is gluten-free for Hashimoto’s (cross-contamination is OK, gluten itself isn’t). Marathon night is at Monja Takarajima specifically because it’s the only Tsukishima monja shop with a gluten-free rice-flour version. Gluten-free requests for Kokuya, Shiga Kogen Prince, and Mayuko’s class are drafted and tracked in Dining and Still Pending.

Can I share this link with anyone?

Share it with family — that’s who it’s for. Please don’t post it publicly: the Flights section includes everyone’s record locators and confirmation details. If someone outside the family needs just one detail, send them that detail rather than the whole link.

What if a plan changes after it’s already on the page?

Send it as an Update using the form above (pick “Update” in the dropdown) with what changed and, if you have it, the new confirmation or time. Once it’s confirmed, the itinerary, lodging, or pending list on this page will be revised to match — the old version won’t stay up alongside it.

When should we re-check the train times?

The transport notes under each day in the itinerary use the routes and typical timings — exact March timetables (especially the Mar 10 Tokyo → Nagano → Shibu legs and the Mar 12 Nagano → Kyoto run) aren’t published yet and should be re-checked in February, when seat reservations are booked.
